title: The body must not have aria-hidden="true"
summary: The body element has aria-hidden="true", which hides the whole page from screen readers. Remove it from the body.
problem: The <body> element has aria-hidden="true". That removes everything on the page from the accessibility tree, so assistive technology sees an empty page. It is usually left behind by a modal or overlay script that failed to clean up.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users can find nothing to read or operate on the page. Content that sighted users see and use is invisible to them.
steps: Find where aria-hidden is set on the body: in your HTML, theme or a script.
If a modal is open and you want to hide the page behind it, set aria-hidden on the individual sections outside the modal, or use the inert attribute, and not on the body.
Make sure your overlay script removes the attribute when the modal closes.

whyItMatters: A page hidden from assistive technology is unusable for the people who depend on it. Because the cause is often a script state, it can appear only after a certain interaction, so it is easy to miss in manual testing. This is a WCAG Level A requirement, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Inspect the body element in your browser and confirm there is no aria-hidden attribute, including after opening and closing any modal. Then re-run the scan.
